name: The Mechanical Age Gazette
bio: Bulletins of the great events of the age. Editorial summaries written for this feed, not a real newspaper.

name: Adam Smith
bio: Late Professor of Moral Philosophy, Glasgow. Author of an Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations.

name: Richard Arkwright
bio: Formerly a barber & wig-maker of Bolton. Patentee of the spinning engine. Proprietor of the mills at Cromford.

name: Matthew Boulton
bio: Toy-maker, button-maker and engine-seller of Soho, near Birmingham. Partner of Mr Watt.

name: James Watt
bio: Mathematical instrument maker, Glasgow. Improver of the fire-engine. Of a melancholy and anxious disposition.

name: Robert Owen
bio: Cotton-spinner & manager of the New Lanark mills. Believes character is formed for man, not by him.

name: General Ned Ludd
bio: Commander of the Army of Redressers. Lives in Sherwood Forest. Nobody has ever seen him.

name: A Huddersfield Cropper
bio: Cloth-dresser. Seven years apprenticed to the shears. Composite voice, reconstructed from Luddite-era records.

name: A Bolton Hand-loom Weaver
bio: Weaver of muslins at my own loom, in my own cottage. Composite voice, reconstructed from weavers' petitions and parliamentary evidence.

name: A Manchester Piecer
bio: Aged nine. Mends broken ends on the mule. Composite voice, reconstructed from factory testimony of 1832–33.

name: A Railway Navvy
bio: Excavator on the Liverpool & Manchester line. Composite voice, reconstructed from contemporary accounts of railway labour.

name: Elizabeth Bentley
bio: Of Leeds. Doffer in a flax mill from the age of six. Witness before Mr Sadler's Committee, 1832.

name: Lord Byron
bio: Peer, poet, Nottinghamshire landowner. Maiden speech in the Lords on the Frame-Work Bill.

name: Percy Bysshe Shelley
bio: Poet. Writing from Italy, where the news from Manchester reaches me late and makes me furious.

name: Samuel Bamford
bio: Weaver & poet of Middleton. Led the Middleton contingent to St Peter's Field. Imprisoned for it.

name: David Ricardo
bio: Stockbroker, MP for Portarlington, political economist. Capable of changing his mind in print.

name: Robert Southey
bio: Poet Laureate. Converses with the ghost of Sir Thomas More on the progress and prospects of society.

name: T. B. Macaulay
bio: Edinburgh Reviewer, Whig MP. We rely on the natural tendency of society to improvement.

name: George Stephenson
bio: Engine-wright of Killingworth. Engineer of the Stockton & Darlington and the Liverpool & Manchester railways.

name: Fanny Kemble
bio: Actress of Covent Garden, on tour in the north. Has ridden on the engine and is a little in love with its engineer.

name: Thomas Creevey
bio: Whig politician & inveterate letter-writer. Guest at Knowsley and Croxteth. Distrusts the loco-motive.

name: Thomas Carlyle
bio: Essayist. Edinburgh Review contributor. Diagnoses the Condition-of-England Question at length.

name: Richard Oastler
bio: Steward of Fixby Hall, Tory, Churchman, and enemy of factory slavery. Called 'the Factory King' by the operatives.

name: Andrew Ure
bio: Chemist, Glasgow. Apologist for the factory system and admirer of the self-acting mule.

name: William Lovett
bio: Cabinet-maker of Cornwall & London. Secretary of the London Working Men's Association. Drafter of the People's Charter.

name: Friedrich Engels
bio: Clerk at Ermen & Engels, cotton-spinners, Manchester. Walks the working-class districts on Sundays.

name: Benjamin Disraeli
bio: Novelist, MP for Shrewsbury, Young Englander. Writes of two nations.

name: Charles Dickens
bio: Novelist. Late of the blacking warehouse. Has seen the black country from a coach window.

name: Elizabeth Gaskell
bio: Minister's wife, Manchester. Visits the homes of the poor of my husband's chapel.

name: Elizabeth Barrett
bio: Poet, of Wimpole Street. Has read Mr Horne's report on the employment of children.

name: Punch
bio: The London Charivari. Founded 1841. Threepence weekly. Mr Punch sees everything.

name: Queen Victoria
bio: By the Grace of God, of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland Queen. Writes often to her dear Uncle Leopold.

name: Prince Albert
bio: President of the Society of Arts. Moving spirit of the Exhibition of the Works of Industry of All Nations.

name: Charlotte Brontë
bio: Author of Jane Eyre and Shirley (a novel of the Luddite year). Of Haworth. Not much in the way of crowds.

name: Henry Mayhew
bio: Journalist, Morning Chronicle correspondent on London labour and the London poor. Co-founder of Punch.

name: John Ruskin
bio: Art critic. Graduate of Oxford. Prefers a crooked Gothic stone made by a free man to a perfect one made by a slave.

name: Samuel Smiles
bio: Surgeon turned editor of the Leeds Times, railway secretary, and biographer of engineers. Heaven helps those who help themselves.
